title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 38
paragraphs: Croesus answered him: “My son, it is not because I have observed in you any spirit of cowardice or any other ungracious thing that I act as I do. But a vision in a dream came and stood beside me in my sleep, and told me that you would be short-lived and that you would perish by an iron spear-point. With this vision in mind I both hastened your marriage, and now I refuse to send you on the undertaking at hand, taking care of you so that I may steal you from your fate—at least for the span of my own life, if by any means possible. For you are, as it happens, my only son: the other I do not reckon as one, since he is deficient in hearing.”
